title: Narrowband searches for continuous gravitational waves from known pulsars in the first two parts of the fourth LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA observing run
extended_summary:
This paper reports results from narrowband searches for continuous gravitational waves from known pulsars during the first two parts of the fourth LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA observing run. It addresses an astrophysical detection problem: whether rotating, non-axisymmetric neutron stars emit continuous gravitational waves that can be observed in the current detector network data.

The work is based on observational data from the LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA gravitational-wave observatories. It is not an education study and does not evaluate an AI intervention, educational tool, learners, or instructional setting. Instead, it analyzes gravitational-wave search methods and observational results for known pulsars.

The paper’s main contribution is to present search findings from the observing run rather than a controlled intervention study. No educational population, user type, training context, or implementation dosage is reported because the paper is outside the requested education domain.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is an astrophysics paper on narrowband searches for continuous gravitational waves from known pulsars, not an education study. There is no educational technology intervention, comparison condition, or learner outcome methodology to evaluate.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational intervention or education-relevant outcomes are reported, so there is no measurable educational impact.
